block.title: OpenSSL's unsigned comparison has a constant-time IR proof
block.p: OpenSSL compares secret unsigned integers without branching on them. The new module page explains how its C function becomes nanofil's optimized IR, then proves that changing the inputs cannot change the execution trace.

claim.p: The compiled comparison never panics or uses a secret in a forbidden operation. Two calls with different secret arguments have the same finite leakage trace under the same runtime driver. Their return values may differ and remain secret. The proof also rejects a branch-based version on less-than, greater-than, and equal inputs.

block.p: This is a proof about generated IR, not native hardware timing or the arithmetic result for all inputs. The fixture check keeps the proof tied to the compiler's current output.
